miniProject.title: Telemetry, a load sweep through the knee, overload control and one incident
miniProject.brief: Make the service slice measurable and upright past capacity with telemetry, a predicted knee, a retained-record load sweep and overload controls. Then inject one incident, recover from the runbook and file the SLO, capacity and postmortem in the dossier.
steps: Instrument every request with identity, trace context, queue, handler and storage timings, status and bounded labels, export raw records with counters and fixed-bucket histograms, and enforce a cardinality budget that fails on an unbounded label.
Predict the knee from measured service time and the queue depth that Little's Law gives at rising fractions of capacity, stating where serialization would lower the prediction.

Sweep rising offered rates with an open-loop Poisson generator that measures from intended send time, keep every raw record across repeats, report percentiles with counts with throughput, queue depth, utilization, errors and recovery, check \(L = \lambda W\), and contrast one closed-loop run.

Add bounded admission, client-side throttling, a per-client retry budget with jittered backoff, a breaker with a stale-marked fallback and deadline propagation, showing each control under the same injected overload.

Write the SLO with availability and latency indicators, budget, alert and shared failure domains, derive capacity now and at higher load with what would shed instead, and gate a versioned canary with automatic rollback, tested with a deliberately slow version.

Inject one incident chosen from a hidden list, work it from telemetry and the runbook with detection to recovery times, restore from the last verified backup with measured recovery and counted loss, and file a blameless postmortem with owned actions and one regression guard.
deliverables: The instrumented service with raw telemetry, the cardinality test and a script rendering percentiles and queue depth.
The prediction with the retained-record sweep, rate table, Little's Law check and closed-loop contrast.
Overload-control and canary comparisons under identical injected faults, and the SLO, capacity, incident and postmortem package.

rubric.pass: Raw records carry identity and timings, the budget test fails on unbounded labels, and the sweep reports percentiles with counts at every rate.
rubric.strong: Percentiles come from raw samples rather than averaged percentiles, and the knee is explained against the prediction.

rubric.pass: Each control is shown under the same overload, and the slow canary triggers automatic rollback.
rubric.strong: Retry and throttle evidence shows a storm contained that a plain retrying client starts.

rubric.pass: The timeline, runbook recovery, measured recovery, counted loss and merged guard are kept with the SLO arithmetic.
rubric.strong: The postmortem is blameless with owned actions, and the plan names shared failure domains and SLO limits.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone dossier: the SLO and capacity estimate against load with the telemetry-based incident. Overload controls stay under test in the service slice.
